source.title: A U-turn on Double Descent: Rethinking Parameter Counting in Statistical Learning
source.authors: Alicia Curth; Alan Jeffares; Mihaela van der Schaar

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study reanalyzes double descent in trees, gradient boosting, and random-feature linear regression. Its results argue that the apparent second descent depends on switching between distinct ways of adding parameters, and is not inherently tied to the interpolation threshold. It explicitly leaves deep double descent for future work.
record.gate_note: The study does not test memorization of random labels, widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, or the optimizer and regularization comparisons in the other versions. The findings below concern non-neural model classes and their test-error curves. Curve values are shown in figures; the text describes their shapes and interpretation but does not give numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study tests explanations of double descent in trees, boosting and random-feature linear regression. None measures widening trained neural networks as V2 specifies. The authors explicitly leave neural-network double descent for future work. Its results therefore do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: for the studied non-neural methods, sequentially traversing distinct parameter-increase mechanisms explains apparent double descent, and using their proposed test-time effective parameter count produces traditional U-shaped curves. The authors leave extension to neural networks for future research.
record.recipe_differences: Reanalyzes and replicates the non-neural tree, boosting, and RFF regression experiments from Belkin et al. (2019), then varies the parameter-increase mechanisms separately and introduces a generalized effective-parameter measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent curve and peak location depend on when the experiments switch between parameter-increase mechanisms (leaf count versus ensemble size; boosting rounds versus ensemble size; fitted PCs versus excess features).

fits_no_version.finding: Tree and boosting experiments yield U- or L-shaped curves along individual parameter axes and apparent double descent when those axes are traversed sequentially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these non-neural models, test-error curves depend on whether added parameters grow individual predictors or ensemble independently trained predictors.

fits_no_version.finding: RFF regression separates into a U-shaped dependence on fitted principal-component count and an L-shaped dependence on excess features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the studied RFF regression setting, additional raw features can improve a fixed-dimensional fitted basis; switching between these mechanisms produces apparent double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Plotting test error against the proposed test-time effective smoother parameter count folds the studied curves into U-shaped contours.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these trees, boosted models and RFF regressions, effective test-time parameter count provides a different complexity description from raw parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Peak-moving experiments produce second descents without interpolation; Proposition 2 also proves identical in-sample prediction error for interpolating predictors under fixed design.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second descent need not coincide with interpolation in these non-neural experiments, while interpolating predictors cannot differ in prediction error evaluated on the same fixed training inputs with new targets.

record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The evidence concerns non-neural methods, not deep networks. Main curve results are presented as plots, and the text gives qualitative shapes rather than point values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. The paper also reports SVHN and CIFAR-10 replications in Appendix E.6, but these are additional figure-only curves for the same three methods and are not separately extracted here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level generalization under random labels in the same neural architectures and recipes.
The entire version: widening trained neural networks beyond zero training error and measuring subsequent test-error changes.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the roles of local connectivity and initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning budgets and recovery through weight decay or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects, small-data and underfitting regimes, and removal of dropout with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V2 verdicts. Non-neural double-descent explanations neither challenge V2's neural-network result nor support it through U-shaped effective-complexity plots. The shared MNIST setting and conceptual connections to neural networks do not establish the required system and operation match.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, widening, and the specified MNIST/downsampled CIFAR-10 settings.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and subsequent test accuracy.

rows.subject: regression trees
rows.operation_detail: Varied terminal-leaf count with ensemble size fixed; test error followed a U- or L-shape.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P leaf
rows.value: Text describes a classical convex U- (or L-) shape; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the curve shape; no point values are stated.
rows.check: Terminal-leaf count in regression trees does not measure neural-network width. The reported U- or L-shaped curves are supported by Section 2.1 but cannot establish V2.

rows.subject: regression trees
rows.operation_detail: Varied number of ensemble members with leaf count fixed; test error followed an L-shape without ascent.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P ens
rows.value: Text describes an L-shape with no ascent; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The paper says adding trees generally does not hurt in this setting.
rows.check: Adding independently trained trees measures ensembling, not widening a neural network. The reported L-shaped curves do not test V2.

rows.subject: regression trees
rows.operation_detail: Connected leaf-count growth to ensemble-size growth on a composite parameter axis, producing an apparent double-descent curve.
rows.measure: Squared test error across composite raw parameter count
rows.value: Text describes an apparent double-descent curve; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The paper attributes the second descent to changing model class/parameter-increase mechanism, not to the interpolation threshold itself.
rows.check: The composite axis switches from growing individual trees to ensembling trees. Apparent double descent is reported, but it is not an incomplete observation of V2.

rows.subject: gradient boosting
rows.operation_detail: Varied boosting rounds with ensemble size fixed; test error followed a U- or L-shape.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P boost
rows.value: Text describes a U- or L-shape; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The result is described qualitatively in the text.
rows.check: Increasing boosting rounds does not measure neural-network width. The stated U- or L-shaped curves cannot establish V2.

rows.subject: gradient boosting
rows.operation_detail: Varied ensemble size with boosting rounds fixed; test error followed an L-shape.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P ens
rows.value: Text describes an L-shape; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The paper says the pattern parallels the tree results.
rows.check: Ensembling independently trained boosted models does not measure widening a neural network.

rows.subject: gradient boosting
rows.operation_detail: Connected growth in boosting rounds to growth in independently ensembled models, producing an apparent double-descent curve.
rows.measure: Squared test error across composite raw parameter count
rows.value: Text describes an apparent double-descent shape; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The authors attribute the shape to switching parameter-increase mechanisms.
rows.check: The composite axis switches from boosting rounds to independent ensembles. Its apparent double descent does not test V2; partial is not an appropriate version-relative state.

rows.subject: RFF linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Varied principal-component count with excess-feature count fixed; test error followed a U-shape.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P PC
rows.value: Text describes a traditional U-shaped curve; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The text says the curve holds for different fixed levels of excess features.
rows.check: Varying retained principal components in RFF linear regression does not measure widening a trained ReLU network.

rows.subject: RFF linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Varied excess features with principal-component count fixed; test error followed an L-shape.
rows.measure: Squared test error across P ex
rows.value: Text describes an L-shaped curve; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as improving the basis used by a fixed-capacity model.
rows.check: Increasing random features while holding fitted principal-component count fixed measures basis enrichment in linear regression, not V2's neural-network widening.

rows.subject: RFF linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Connected growth in fitted principal components to growth in excess features, producing apparent double descent.
rows.measure: Squared test error across composite raw parameter count
rows.value: Text describes apparent double descent; precise values figure only.
rows.note: The paper says the transition naturally occurs at P φ = n for this procedure, but the peak location can be shifted by changing where the mechanism switches.
rows.check: The composite principal-component/excess-feature axis concerns linear regression. Apparent double descent is reported, but it is not a partial observation of V2.

rows.subject: regression trees, gradient boosting, and RFF linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalized effective parameter count on test inputs and plotted test error against that measure.
rows.measure: Squared test error versus test-time effective parameter count ptest_ŝ
rows.value: Text says the apparent double-descent curves fold back into convex U-shapes; precise values figure only.
rows.note: Figure 9 plots the three methods separately; the text reports the shared qualitative pattern.
rows.check: Effective smoother parameter count is not neural-network width or magnitude-aware sharpness. Figure 9 concerns the MNIST 0-versus-all subproblem, rather than summed error across all ten classes. Its three model families should be separate rows.
